options: A GUI application only available on Windows and Mac
The core background daemon that builds images and runs containers, plus the docker CLI
A cloud service for storing container images
A Kubernetes distribution bundled with Docker Desktop
questions.explain: Docker Engine is the core piece of Docker: the daemon that actually builds images and runs containers, along with the docker command-line client.

questions.q: Why does Docker Desktop add a managed Linux virtual machine on Windows and Mac, but not on Linux?
options: Because Docker Desktop is buggy on Linux
Because Windows and macOS can't run Linux containers natively, while Linux can run them directly on its own kernel
Because Linux containers require more resources than Windows containers
Because Docker Engine does not exist for Linux
questions.explain: Linux can run Linux containers natively, since they share its kernel. Windows and macOS need a Linux VM under the hood to provide that kernel, which Docker Desktop manages automatically.

questions.q: Which command installs Docker Desktop on Windows using the built-in package manager?
options: apt install docker-desktop
winget install -e --id Docker.DockerDesktop
brew install --cask docker-desktop
docker install desktop --windows
questions.explain: On Windows, winget (Windows Package Manager) installs Docker Desktop with `winget install -e --id Docker.DockerDesktop`.

questions.q: On Linux, why do most developers install Docker Engine directly instead of using Docker Desktop?
options: Docker Desktop doesn't support the docker CLI
Linux runs containers natively on its own kernel, so no managed VM or Desktop GUI layer is required
Docker Engine cannot run on Linux without Desktop
Linux requires a completely different tool than docker
questions.explain: Because Linux already provides the kernel features containers need, Docker Engine alone -- installed via the official apt repository -- is sufficient; no Desktop VM layer is necessary.

questions.q: What does seeing the "Hello from Docker!" message after running `docker run hello-world` confirm?
options: That your internet connection is working, nothing more
That the Docker daemon is running and the docker CLI can successfully reach it
That Docker Desktop has been uninstalled
That you have administrator privileges on the host machine
questions.explain: `docker run hello-world` pulls and runs a tiny test image specifically to confirm the Docker daemon is running and reachable from the CLI.
